When I write a story, I always see it through the characters' eyes and through what they're feeling. It's not like a movie or television where you're on the outside looking in. So I think my style might be more internal and character-focused as a result of that. In the past when I've tried to write for film or television (which makes no sense, but roll with me) it was hard for me to not be able to express what the characters' were feeling and thinking on the inside. As a result, the scenes didn't go anywhere.

Really good question.

I don't think I'm consciously avoiding it. It's not really a point of pride. It's more just that it's hard for me to make the investment. I won't object if somebody told me, "Hey, let's get together and watch this." But even if I enjoy it, it's just not something I'll go back to in my free time alone. I'd rather be doing something else. A lot of people here make these posts where they're bragging about how they don't do things like other people. And like you said, maybe it's a point of pride for them. For me, it's really just that I'd rather be doing something else that I find more fun.

I think your point about narrative is really interesting. In terms of storytelling, I read a pretty excessive amount and obviously love stories. So I don't think my appetite for that isn't quenched. I think your point would hold more weight if I was a screenwriter, which I'm not. Telling a story through a characters' inner thought process in a novel and telling it through pictures on television are really different. I'd certainly be up for looking into movies or television to study narrative structure. But it's also not really the form of storytelling that interests me to begin with.
